title: 4 mistakes people make when testing AI trading bots (and why they blow up in live markets)
author: DTAKthatGuy
selftext:
Testing a normal indicator (like a Moving Average or RSI) is easy because math doesn't have a memory.

Testing an **AI trading agent** is a whole different game. If you test an AI the same way you test a normal bot, you will get amazing test results that immediately lose money in the real market.

Here are the 4 biggest traps to avoid when testing AI in trading:

* **Trap #1: Testing on dates the AI already memorized.** If an AI model finished training in December 2024, testing it on 2023 charts is useless. It already knows who won and who lost in 2023. Always test on fresh data *after* its training cutoff.
* **Trap #2: Leaving ticker names visible.** If the AI sees "AAPL" or "TSLA" in the data or news feed, its past memory kicks in. You have to disguise the asset as "ASSET\_A" and convert dollar prices into basic percentages.
* **Trap #3: Testing on a basic spreadsheet.** AI agents interact with the market step-by-step. You can't test them on a static sheet—you have to feed the AI one candle at a time, and factor in the 300–500ms it takes for the AI to "think" before buying at the Ask price.
* **Trap #4: Relying only on real history.** The smartest way to test an AI is throwing it into computer-generated (synthetic) market charts that mimic real crashes and volatility. If it survives markets that never happened in history, the strategy actually works.
